title: Next-gen multimodal large model cuts cost of lung cancer genetic testing
key_facts: DeepGEM 2.0, a multimodal large AI model for lung cancer pathological genomics, was released in Guangzhou on Saturday (10 Oct 2026).
It was developed jointly by the First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University and the testing company Guangzhou KingMed Diagnostics Group.
It does image-based gene recognition in as little as one minute and, according to the company, can pre-screen for gene targets that match lung cancer targeted therapies already approved in China.
A multicentre research project at 50 medical institutions has been launched, which marks the model's entry into large-scale clinical validation; the model is planned for use in over 500 institutions.
Liang Wenhua, vice-president of the hospital, says AI pre-screening plus specific gene-targeted verification is expected to cut the cost of lung cancer genetic testing to a few hundred yuan.
Liu Si, head of the AI special project at KingMed Diagnostics, says the new version's prediction accuracy can reach up to 90 percent.
The first generation (2025) takes pathology slides as input and predicts the probability of lung cancer-related gene mutations and where they sit in the tissue.
quote_evidence: The DeepGEM 2.0, jointly developed by the First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University and Guangzhou KingMed Diagnostics Group, a testing company, achieves image-based gene recognition in as little as one minute.

By relying on AI pre-screening and specific gene-targeted verification, the technology is expected to reduce the cost of lung cancer genetic testing to a few hundred yuan, Liang Wenhua, vice-president of the First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University, said.
The prediction accuracy of the model's new version can reach up to 90 percent, Liu Si, head of the AI special project at KingMed Diagnostics, said.
why_it_matters_hint: If the cost claim holds, targeted-therapy gene testing could reach more lung cancer patients at local hospitals, but the figures are the developers' own and validation has just started.
event_date: Released on Saturday 10 Oct 2026 (China Daily article dated 10 Oct 2026)
notes: Read China Daily in full. Cost reduction is stated as expected, not achieved; accuracy and cost figures come from the hospital and KingMed, with no outside review reported.
